body: Chief: take bd-01M15XZ290HDMPTA4NXP88G4CM, align/population typed error cases and smart-constructed receipt, moved off m1 which is holding five items while you are free. Three parts, all from the scout's review: (1) STOP REUSING AlignError.FingerprintMismatch for population member mismatches - it means a fingerprint carried ON THE WIRE, and population uses it for an in-memory proof-versus-aggregate mismatch with the subject id smuggled into a String field, which the TESTS THEN PARSE with startsWith and contains. Dedicated typed cases: PopulationViewMismatch(subject, proof, aggregate) and PopulationRecallMismatch(subject, proof, suppliedRecall). (2) PopulationReceipt's four independent public fields can be constructed inconsistently, and sorting checksums independently destroys the subject-to-recall binding; smart-construct over a sorted NonEmptyVector[PopulationMemberReceipt(subject, recallChecksum, unitPresence)] and DERIVE the counts. (3) Rename contentlessSubjects to subjectsWithNoRecallUnits - the predicate is recall.units.isEmpty, which does NOT establish that a participant was silent; it can equally mean nothing was segmented, and the fixture proves it by using non-empty text with zero units. I approved the wrong word originally. ONE WARNING FROM TONIGHT that applies directly: m1's Conditional type was blocked because a case class exposes _1, productElement, unapply and copy, and its compile-time tripwire only guarded the names it had imagined. If you smart-construct PopulationReceipt, make it a non-case class with a private constructor, and check toString too - a logged payload is an unconditional read that no accessor test will catch.
